title: NFS server (shire)
description: shire as an NFS server: requests, delegations, clients, and the shire and shiren filesystems.

panels.title: Requests
panels.description: NFS requests (RPC calls) per second over the last 5 minutes, every transport and client.

panels.title: TEST_STATEID share
panels.description: TEST_STATEID operations as a percent of NFSv4.1 requests (one SEQUENCE each) over the last 5 minutes. A client tests its stateids when the server flags that some of its state was revoked. Normally near 0; it was 65% averaged since shire last booted (Oct 2026).

panels.title: Delegations held
panels.description: Delegations shire has handed out and not had back, per filesystem (read and write).

panels.title: Recalls
panels.description: Delegations shire has asked a client to give back and is still waiting for (sampled every minute). Usually 0: clients answer quickly. A count that persists means clients are slow or not answering recalls, which is how delegations end up revoked.

panels.title: Threads in D
panels.description: nfsd threads in uninterruptible sleep, usually waiting on the disks. Requests queue once all 256 threads are busy.

panels.title: Space used
panels.description: Share of each exported filesystem in use.

panels.title: RDMA clients
panels.description: Clients with at least one NFS-over-RDMA connection to shire.

panels.title: State management operations
panels.description: Operations per second at the server, from every client (log scale). A client sends TEST_STATEID to check its state after the server flags some of it revoked, and FREE_STATEID to clear revoked state; many tests with few frees is a client looping on revoked state. DELEGRETURN is a delegation handed back, OPEN for scale.

panels.title: TEST_STATEID share of requests
panels.description: TEST_STATEID operations as a percent of NFSv4.1 requests (one SEQUENCE each).

panels.title: Delegations held
panels.description: Delegations shire has handed out, per filesystem (read solid, write dashed), from /proc/locks every minute. Which client holds them is root-only.

panels.title: TEST_STATEID by client
panels.description: TEST_STATEID per second to shire and shiren. arnor and gondor from their own NFS client counters; other clients is the server's total minus those (rivendell, rohan1-3, annwn, epyc, the service VMs, ...). Per-client state on the server is root-only, so this is as close as an unprivileged check gets to who is storming. 5-minute resolution (the clients' check interval).

panels.title: DELEGRETURN by client
panels.description: Delegations handed back per second to shire and shiren, split the same way as TEST_STATEID. A sustained high rate is delegation churn.

panels.title: Recalls in progress
panels.description: Delegations being recalled at each sample: the server asked for them back and is waiting (up to 45 s, lease-break-time) for the client.

panels.title: Files with shared delegations
panels.description: Files with read delegations held by more than one client. One write to such a file recalls every one of them at once.

panels.title: Stale file handles
panels.description: Requests per second answered with a stale file handle (the file was removed or the export changed under the client), per client. A green "none" line at 0 when there were none.

panels.title: Operations by type
panels.description: NFSv4 operations per second by type. Leaves out SEQUENCE (one per request) and TEST_STATEID (on its own panel, it would dwarf the rest) and the file handle bookkeeping every request carries. OTHER is everything else (SETATTR, RENAME, REMOVE, LOCK, ...). The kernel counts these for the whole server, not per export.

panels.title: Data read and written
panels.description: Bytes per second clients read from and wrote to shire, both filesystems.

panels.title: Requests by transport
panels.description: Requests per second over RDMA and TCP. Most clients mount over RDMA; the service VMs (including this one) mount over TCP.

panels.title: nfsd threads busy
panels.description: nfsd threads at each sample: waiting in D (usually on the disks) or running. Idle threads are in I. When all are busy, requests wait for a free thread.

panels.title: Thread wakeups
panels.description: From /proc/fs/nfsd/pool_stats: requests arriving and nfsd threads woken to handle them, per second. Timed out is a thread that waited for work and got none (an idle server).

panels.title: Bad requests
panels.description: Requests nfsd rejected (malformed, failed authentication, or from an unknown client), per second. Normally 0.

panels.title: Data read by client
panels.description: Bytes per second read per client and filesystem, from /proc/fs/nfsd/export_stats. Each entry restarts from zero when the export cache refreshes it, so a sample is occasionally missing.

panels.title: Data written by client
panels.description: Bytes per second written per client and filesystem, from /proc/fs/nfsd/export_stats. Each entry restarts from zero when the export cache refreshes it, so a sample is occasionally missing.

panels.title: Connections by client
panels.description: Open connections to nfsd per client: RDMA (one per connection; arnor and gondor use 8 each) and TCP to port 2049. A line ending means the client disconnected; a dip and recovery is a reconnect.

panels.title: Storage: shire (/data, MegaRAID) and shiren (/nvme, NVMe RAID0)
I/O operations: shire
panels.description: Reads and writes per second on shire's block device.

panels.title: Throughput: shire
panels.description: Bytes per second read from and written to shire's block device.

panels.title: Wait per I/O: shire
panels.description: Average time per read and per write on shire's block device, queueing included.

panels.title: Busy: shire
panels.description: Share of time shire's disks had I/O in flight: each NVMe drive for shiren, the one MegaRAID volume for shire (whose drives the kernel can't see; 100% there doesn't mean every drive is busy).

targets.expr: rate(node_disk_io_time_seconds_total{host="shire", fs="shire", level="member"}[$__rate_interval]) or (rate(node_disk_io_time_seconds_total{host="shire", fs="shire", level="volume"}[$__rate_interval]) unless on (fs) node_disk_io_time_seconds_total{host="shire", fs="shire", level="member"})

panels.title: XFS journal: shire
panels.description: Per second: log forces (waits for the journal to reach disk, from fsync and NFS COMMIT), the ones that had to sleep, and transactions stalled because the journal was full (normally 0).

panels.title: Space and inodes used: shire
panels.description: Share of shire's space (available to users) and inodes in use.

panels.title: I/O operations: shiren
panels.description: Reads and writes per second on shiren's block device.

panels.title: Throughput: shiren
panels.description: Bytes per second read from and written to shiren's block device.

panels.title: Wait per I/O: shiren
panels.description: Average time per read and per write on shiren's block device, queueing included.

panels.title: Busy: shiren
panels.description: Share of time shiren's disks had I/O in flight: each NVMe drive for shiren, the one MegaRAID volume for shire (whose drives the kernel can't see; 100% there doesn't mean every drive is busy).

targets.expr: rate(node_disk_io_time_seconds_total{host="shire", fs="shiren", level="member"}[$__rate_interval]) or (rate(node_disk_io_time_seconds_total{host="shire", fs="shiren", level="volume"}[$__rate_interval]) unless on (fs) node_disk_io_time_seconds_total{host="shire", fs="shiren", level="member"})

panels.title: XFS journal: shiren
panels.description: Per second: log forces (waits for the journal to reach disk, from fsync and NFS COMMIT), the ones that had to sleep, and transactions stalled because the journal was full (normally 0).

panels.title: Space and inodes used: shiren
panels.description: Share of shiren's space (available to users) and inodes in use.

panels.title: RDMA errors and retransmissions
panels.description: Events per second from shire's RDMA adapter (mlx5_bond_0), all clients together. packet_seq_err and out_of_sequence: packets lost or reordered on the way in. roce_adp_retrans: shire retransmitting. *_cqe_error and *_remote_access_errors: failed operations. The same counters on arnor and gondor (Hosts overview) show the other end of each link. A green "no errors" line at 0 when nothing moved.

panels.title: RDMA congestion and receive drops
panels.description: Per second: congestion notifications shire sent (np_cnp_sent) and acted on (rp_cnp_handled), packets that arrived ECN-marked by the switch, requests a client repeated (duplicate_request), and packets dropped because nfsd hadn't posted a receive buffer in time (out_of_buffer: shire falling behind). A green "none" line at 0 when nothing moved.
